subject: Dedicated capacity: inference load portrait & sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@elevara.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — baseline traffic and peak bursts

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for taking the intro call last week. We wanted to move the conversation toward sizing for a Dedicated deployment. High level: Elevara is building an agent platform for retail support with a mix of short and long-turn prompts. Before we lock in a workshop, could you point us to the exact fields you need filled to get an initial GPU footprint estimate? Below are some early numbers on our side — please tell us what else is required.

Quick snapshot:
- Expected daily active requests: ~120k
- Average prompts / request: 1.2 (most are single-turn Q/A; ~8% multi-turn)
- Prompt tokens (median): 45 tokens
- Completion tokens (median): 220 tokens
- Percent of requests requiring streaming output: 35% (conversational replies with step-by-step)
- 99th percentile latency target: 350ms for standard routes; 150ms for VIP routes (checkout)

We will need commitment guidance and any guardrails that meaningfully change the SKU mix (e.g., session affinity, long-kept KV cache). Happy to complete a questionnaire if you can send one.

Best,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering
Elevara

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — baseline traffic and peak bursts

Hi Alex / Samantha,

Thanks — that snapshot is very helpful. I attached a short pre-sales sizing questionnaire we usually ask customers to complete; it’s deliberately focused on signal that changes GPU mix and commitment size. If you can fill items 1–6 we can produce an initial Dedicated footprint (SKU / GPU count / expected concurrency) within 48 hours.

Key items in the form (quick summary):
1) Request distribution by route (checkout / search / help / async batch) — percent of total
2) Peak QPS (minute-level) and sustained QPS (hour-level) for each route
3) Token distribution percentiles (p50, p90, p99) for prompt and completion
4) Session duration and KV cache hit rate assumptions (do sessions persist across minutes/hours?)
5) Ratios of streaming vs non-streaming, and whether partial token batching is acceptable
6) SLA priorities: which routes need VIP latency vs cost-optimized handling

Two quick clarifications from your snapshot:
- When you say 120k daily active requests, is that active unique users or total API calls?
- For the 35% streaming, are you using server-side chunking today or client pulls?

I’ve looped in Marissa (pre-sales sizing lead) and Karthik (model-ops) — they’ll validate assumptions around quantization/kv-cache.

I attached: "pre_sales_dedicated_sizing_form.xlsx" (stub) and a short example output from a similar mid-market retail customer for reference.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Forwarding the draft responses — we filled the form inline below. Let us know if anything looks inconsistent.

--- Form answers (condensed):
1) Route split:
   - Checkout (high priority): 15%
   - Search / Product Q: 50%
   - Help / Long form: 25%
   - Batch async (post-process): 10%
2) Peak QPS: 1,800 QPS total (peak minute), sustained 350 QPS (hourly average)
   - Checkout peak: 600 QPS at 1300–1400 PST peak window
3) Token percentiles (prompt / completion): p50: 40/180, p90: 80/420, p99: 160/1,200
4) Session: average session 6 minutes, KV cache hit rate ~22% (short-lived context per shopper)
5) Streaming: server-side chunking for checkout and long-form; streaming allowed to be prioritized but not required for search
6) SLA priorities: Checkout (latency), Search (throughput/cost), Help (quality)

Other notes: we expect a 4x spike for flash sale events (approx 2–3 hours, once per quarter). We attached a sample minute-level trace for last Black Friday as CSV.

Best,
Samantha
Senior Product Manager, Elevara

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: inference load portrait & sizing clarifications

Thanks for the detail, Samantha — excellent data. A few internal action items / assumptions I want to confirm before we produce the footprint: 

- Sliding windows & burst handling: for the 4x flash sale spike, do you expect uniform increase across all routes or mostly Checkout/Search? If mostly Checkout, we will size a small pool of VIP nodes with reserved slots + autoscale bursts.
- KV cache behavior: 22% hit rate is low; that pushes us to model a higher average GPU memory utilization per session since cold starts will re-run more context.
- Quantization profile: to hit the 150ms VIP target at p99 for Checkout we’ll likely recommend int8 quantization with a latency-optimized kernel (model permitting) — will Elevara accept a minor quality delta in exchange for lower cost?

Next steps: I’ll run the input through our sizing engine and share a draft SKU matrix (GPU types, counts, and expected concurrency) by EOD. Rachel — can you prepare a short canary+fallback plan (one-pager) we can include in the MA Plan?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole

Alex / Samantha — thanks for the quick turnaround and the trace file. Attached is a short draft "Mutual Action Plan" and a one-page canary + fallback sketch that outlines: reserved VIP pool for Checkout, autoscale policy for Search, and a degraded-mode path that routes non-VIP work to a cost tier during flash spikes.

We flagged the quantization tradeoff as a decision point for the kickoff — if you are open to an A/B quality test we can measure the delta on a subset of traffic during the pilot. If not, we’ll propose a larger GPU count to meet latency with the non-quantized model.

Next: Marissa will post the SKU matrix within 6 hours; we can schedule a kick-off sizing workshop next week to finalize commitment.

Please confirm a preferred 60–90 minute slot next Thursday or Friday for the workshop.

Best,
Rachel Kim
